In [[cryptography]], '''SHARK''' is a [[block cipher]] identified as one of the predecessors of [[Rijndael]] (the [[Advanced Encryption Standard]]).

SHARK has a 64-bit [[block size (cryptography)|block size]] and a 128-bit [[key size]]. It is a six-round [[substitution–permutation network|SP-network]] which alternates a [[key (cryptography)|key]] mixing stage with linear and non-linear transformation layers. The linear transformation uses an [[MDS matrix]] representing a [[Reed–Solomon error correction|Reed–Solomon]] [[error correcting code]] in order to guarantee good [[confusion and diffusion|diffusion]]. The nonlinear layer is composed of eight 8×8-bit [[S-box]]es based on the function ''F(x) = x<sup>−1</sup>'' over ''GF(2<sup>8</sup>)''.

Five rounds of a modified version of SHARK can be broken using an [[interpolation attack]] (Jakobsen and Knudsen, 1997).
